newsitem.title: UK: McDonnell Info sees substantial loss for '96.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Info sees substantial loss for '96.

text.p: Britain's McDonnell Information Systems Plc said on Thursday it expected to post "very substantial" losses for 1996 due to provisions for software development contracts.
The firm said it had cut its estimates for the year as a result of its decision to make full provision in its 1996 accounts against the future costs of the contracts.
McDonnell also said it hired Close Brothers to advise on an expected refinancing of the company.
McDonnell Information's shares sank 24 percent, dropping 8.0p to 26 by 0800 GMT to rank among the top percentage losers on the London Stock Exchange.
The company said it expected a sustained improvement in operating performance in the current year.
"Trading since the 1996 year-end has been on a rising trend, especially in the core UK corporate and public sector businesses," McDonnell said in its statement.
Regarding its new software joint venture with Japan's Fujitsu Ltd, McDonnell said it would hold an initial 64 percent stake in the partnership.

McDonnell said it would transfer its Chess business in the U.S. into the new venture, called Glovia International LLC, while Fujitsu will contribute $25 million in cash and certain software assets worth about $4.0 million in exchange for a 36 percent stake.
Subject to performance targets, McDonnell will transfer its UK and Continental European Chess businesses into Glovia before 1999 and increase its stake to 69.5 percent.
But Fujitsu will have the right from February 1, 1999, to increase its interest in Glovia to 51 percent.
McDonnell's Chess products include open systems applications software that enables businesses to plan and control their functions.

Glovia, based in California, will develop package software for manufacturing companies' production and sales control and have a staff of about 230, Fujitsu said earlier. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
